principles.statement: Optimize pronunciation for intelligibility first and comprehensibility second; never use accentedness or native-likeness alone as a failure criterion.
Use Vietnamese population findings as diagnostic priors, then require learner-level evidence before allocating substantial pronunciation practice.
Near A0, prioritize preservation of information-bearing word shape—especially risky codas and clusters—before fine accent polish when learner evidence confirms the problem.
Give extra priority to pronunciation deviations that erase lexical or grammatical information, while keeping feature-specific evidence boundaries explicit.
Use functional load as one ranking signal for segmental contrasts, not as a universal Vietnamese phoneme curriculum.
Prioritize lexical-stress correction when the deviation damages vowel/syllable realization or word identification; do not correct every harmless prominence difference.
Teach vowel contrasts diagnostically around lexical information and actual learner/listener confusion rather than requiring one native-accent vowel inventory.
Use sentence focus, timing and intonation where they reduce listener effort or carry communicative intent; do not impose native-like rhythm as an A0 accent badge.
Embed pronunciation work inside meaningful listening/speaking tasks and require model-hidden changed-context production before claiming independent pronunciation transfer.
Record target-feature realization, listener intelligibility, comprehensibility, support and scoring provenance separately rather than collapsing them into one pronunciation score.
Sample pronunciation outcomes across more than one relevant listener background before treating a target as broadly communication-critical.
If speech is reliably understood, do not force correction solely to erase a Vietnamese accent; optional accent refinement must remain learner-controlled.
Do not use ASR/vendor pronunciation scores as mastery gates until RQ-008 validates them against intended human listener outcomes for this population and task.
Calibrate pronunciation target ordering by delayed first-seen listener understanding gained per learner minute, not by immediate imitation accuracy alone.
